rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes '2' to '3' at line 49, which is inside a comment string: '// Reduce over dim2 (dimension 2)' becomes '// Reduce over dim3 (dimension 2)'. Comments have no effect on program execution. All actual kernel code, indexing calculations, and reduction logic remain identical.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation targets a numeric character inside a comment string, not an actual numeric constant used in computation. The const_perturb mutation operator incorrectly identified the '2' in the string 'dim2' within the comment as a numeric constant to perturb. Since C++ compilers completely ignore comments during compilation, the generated machine code is identical between original and mutant. Layer 2 testing confirmed bitwise equivalence across 112 test rounds including diverse stress patterns, which is expected because the computation is literally identical. No input value can distinguish between these two versions because they produce the exact same compiled code.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation only affects a comment, which has no effect on computation. The original and mutant produce identical compiled code and thus identical outputs for all possible inputs.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should exclude comments from mutation targets, as comment mutations always produce equivalent mutants. The const_perturb operator should be refined to only target numeric constants in executable code, not numeric characters appearing in string literals or comments.
